en-US.author: Adam Skowroński
en-US.description: Windows desktop app for downloading videos via yt-dlp, with a bundled FFmpeg for post-processing.
en-US.longDescription: VideoDownloader is a Windows desktop app for downloading videos via yt-dlp, with a bundled custom FFmpeg for merging and remuxing. Paste a link or a list of links, pick a video/audio quality or let it auto-select the best available, and queue batch downloads with configurable concurrency, per-job progress, and cancel support. Every attempt is logged to a searchable download history with one-click redownload. Available in English and Polish, with Light/Dark/System UI themes.
en-US.name: VideoDownloader
en-US.releaseNotes:
Windows desktop app for downloading videos via yt-dlp, with a bundled custom FFmpeg for post-processing/remuxing.
What's new since v0.7.0
- Fixed: videos with multiple audio tracks / HLS streams failed to download. YouTube's HLS (m3u8) formats - e.g. the original-language and auto-dubbed audio tracks on multi-language videos - couldn't be merged by the bundled FFmpeg. It now includes the MPEG-TS and AAC demuxers needed for them.
- Fixed: VP9 (webm) video saved as MP4 produced files that wouldn't open. The bundled FFmpeg now probes VP9 streams correctly, so the MP4 gets a valid codec configuration. Streams are still copied, never re-encoded.
- Fixed: failed downloads were shown as completed. If yt-dlp reports an error, the job is now marked as failed with the actual error message (also in the download history), instead of a bogus "Completed" entry with no file size.
- The app version is now shown in the main window's title bar.
- The MSI installer no longer bundles unnecessary non-Windows runtime files.
- Now available on winget: winget install APPIT.VideoDownloader
Requirements: Windows, .NET 8 Desktop Runtime.
Run VideoDownloader-0.7.1-Setup.msi to install, download VideoDownloader-v0.7.1-win-x64.zip, extract, and run VideoDownloader.Wpf.exe for a portable copy, or install with winget install APPIT.VideoDownloader.
